what_its_for: Pirfenidone is used to treat a lung disease called idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). IPF causes scar tissue to build up in your lungs over time, making it harder to breathe. This medicine helps slow down the scarring and may help you breathe better for longer.
how_to_take: Take pirfenidone by mouth with food. Always take it with a meal to help reduce stomach upset and nausea. Swallow the capsules or tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or break them. Take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over 3 weeks to help your body get used to the medicine. The usual starting dose is 267 mg (one capsule or tablet) three times a day with meals for the first week. In the second week, it increases to 534 mg (two capsules or tablets) three times a day. By the third week and beyond, the full dose is 801 mg (three capsules or tablets) three times a day with meals. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how well you tolerate it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember IF it is still close to the time of your usual meal. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one as planned. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store pirfenidone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place such as a dresser drawer or cabinet — NOT in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking, as it can make your lung disease worse and may reduce how well this medicine works. Avoid or limit grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the level of pirfenidone in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds, because pirfenidone can make your skin much more sensitive to sunlight (photosensitivity). When going outside, use sunscreen with SPF 50 or higher, wear protective clothing, and wear a hat. Avoid fluvoxamine (a medicine used for depression or OCD) while taking pirfenidone, and always tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe or worsening shortness of breath or chest pain, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) or dark urine (signs of liver problems), severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that does not go away, a severe skin rash, blistering, or sunburn reaction, signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty swallowing, dizziness or loss of balance that affects your daily activities, or any new or unusual symptoms that concern you. Also contact your doctor if side effects like nausea, diarrhea, or fatigue are making it hard for you to take your medicine — your dose may need to be adjusted.
when_it_works: Pirfenidone does not cure IPF, but it works to slow the progression of lung scarring. You may not feel an immediate difference when you start taking it. The benefits build up over months of consistent use. Some people notice they are not getting worse as quickly, while others may see small improvements in breathing tests. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you do not notice obvious changes, because it is working to protect your lungs over the long term. Talk to your doctor if you have questions about how your treatment is going.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Pirfenidone can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and stomach problems. Monitor closely and report any concerns to your doctor. Kidney problems: If you have mild to moderate kidney disease, your doctor may use this medicine with caution. It is generally not recommended for people with severe kidney disease. Let your doctor know about any kidney issues. Liver problems: Pirfenidone can affect the liver. It should be used with caution in people with liver disease, and it may not be recommended if you have severe liver problems. Your doctor will likely do blood tests to check your liver function regularly. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if pirfenidone is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. Children: Pirfenidone is not approved for use in children.
